# Intake Brief: Achievement give-aways — unlock three games when achievements are achieved

## Problem statement

To reward engaged players, three games from the TCE catalog will be given away free when players achieve certain achievements in the Steam launcher. The unlock uses the **same game-agnostic mechanism** as the free game awarded for following on Steam (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC): bundled content locked by default, unlocked in place, persisted across launches.

## Users

- **Steam players** — earn free games as a reward for reaching achievements; a reason to keep playing.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — a growth/engagement mechanic that drives play without manual key distribution.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want a free game to unlock in my launcher once I've won my first game and reached one more milestone, so my progress is rewarded.
- As a publisher, I want achievement give-aways delivered through the existing bundled-content/unlock architecture, so no manual key handling is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Three games are selected** from the TCE catalog for achievement give-away; the selection is a documented business decision (Main Street is a noted candidate; selection avoids overlap with the follow-on-Steam bonus game choice — see Related work) and the chosen set + rationale is recorded in the item/design doc.
2. Each give-away game unlocks when the player achieves its configured trigger achievements: **"win your first game" plus one additional achievement** (suggested: first win in a second distinct game — final choice recorded, see Appendix). Trigger definitions live in one config (achievement ids → game id) and are game-agnostic.
3. The unlock uses **the same mechanism as the follow-on-Steam free game** (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC): bundled content, locked by default, unlocked in place, persisted across launches, game-agnostic unlock logic.
4. Unlock state persists across launches; re-checks on demand; graceful degradation when Steam/Steamworks is absent (CTA/lock state degrades without crashing the app).
5. Trigger achievements come from the engine-generic achievement layer (CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ): give-away config consumes achievement-unlock events, not game-specific hacks.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Reuse, don't reinvent:** the unlock mechanism (bundled-content unlock, persistence, game-agnostic design) is the one designed in CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC; this item adds achievement-triggered unlocks as an additional trigger source on the same path.
- **Game selection is a business decision** and part of this item's scope (user: "don't know yet (note Main Street)").
- **Dependencies:** blocked by CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ (achievements exist as engine-generic events) and CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC (unlock mechanism). Both are prerequisites for implementation.
- **Trigger achievements:** "win your first game" plus one more (user decision; second achievement suggested — final choice to be confirmed).
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies.
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).

## Existing state

- Follow-on-Steam item (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC, intake_complete) designs the game-agnostic free-game unlock: Steamworks-based follow detection + local unlock persistence + bundled DLC content; **not yet implemented** — this item should coordinate so the unlock path is shared.
- No achievement system exists yet; CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ (challenges → Steam achievements, engine-generic) is the event source this item consumes.
- Game catalog (`main.ts` GAMES): Gym (demos), 9-Card Golf, Beleaguered Castle, Sushi Go!, Feudalism, Lost Cities, Main Street, Blackjack, Coloretto. Steam launcher (CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW) will bundle a subset with DLC architecture.
- CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC has an open question: which game is the designated free follow-bonus (business decision, game-agnostic ACs) — give-away selection must not conflict with it.

## Desired change

1. **Select and document the three give-away games** (business decision; Main Street noted as a candidate; rationale recorded).
2. Define the **trigger config** (achievement ids from CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ's manifest → unlocked game id) in one place (e.g. `electron/achievement-giveaways.ts`).
3. **Extend the shared unlock mechanism** from CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC to accept achievement-triggered unlocks (same persistence/unlock path; new trigger source alongside the follow trigger).
4. **UI:** locked give-away games shown in the Game Selector with unlock progress (which trigger achievements remain); unlocked games become playable.
5. Tests (mocked trigger source + unlock persistence; headless unit tests) + documentation.

## Key Files

- `electron/achievement-giveaways.ts` (new) — give-away config: trigger achievement ids → game id; selection rationale comment.
- `electron/` unlock module from CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC — extended with the achievement trigger source (shared path, game-agnostic).
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` (or launcher UI module) — locked state + unlock progress display for give-away games.
- Achievement manifest from CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ — the trigger ids referenced by the config.
- `tests/` — unit tests for trigger evaluation and unlock persistence with mocked sources.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md` — give-away configuration and QA workflow documentation.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC – Follow-on-Steam incentive: unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher** (open, intake_complete) — the unlock mechanism this item reuses; its open question on the follow-bonus game choice must be coordinated with give-away selection.
- **CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ – Challenges as achievements: sync in-game challenges to Steam achievements** (open, idea) — the engine-generic achievement event source; blocked-by for this item.
- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, plan_complete) — the Steam version hosting both features.
- `main.ts` GAMES catalog — the candidate pool for the three give-away games.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ and CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC land first; this item's implementation is gated on both.
- **Assumption:** The three give-away games are chosen from the current catalog; Main Street is a candidate (user note).
- **Risk:** Conflict between the follow-on-Steam bonus game and the give-away set (e.g. same game twice, or devaluing the follow incentive) — mitigation: selection and rationale recorded, coordinated with the follow-item's open question.
- **Risk:** If the achievement layer (CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ) is delayed, the trigger source is missing — mitigation: define the trigger config/interface in this item early, independent of Steam sync internals.
- **Scope-creep risk:** trading cards, seasonal give-aways, paid DLC sales, and anti-abuse (achievement-farm detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Do you already have the three games in mind, or should the work item include evaluating/selecting them from the catalog (e.g. Main Street, Golf, Blackjack…)?"
  — Answer (user): "don't know yet (note Main Street)". Source: interactive reply (2026-08-09). Implication: selection is a deliverable of this item; Main Street is a recorded candidate.
- Q2: "Should the give-away unlock on specific milestone achievements (e.g. 'complete all challenges in a game', 'win your first game'), or on any achievement being reached?"
  — Answer (user): "win your first game plus one other (suggest)". Source: interactive reply (2026-08-09). **Suggested second achievement: "win your first game in a second distinct game"** (rewards breadth of play; both triggers are engine-generic and achievable without the give-away game itself). Alternative candidates: "complete your first full game" (reach a game-over screen without quitting) or "complete all challenges in any game". Final choice to be confirmed at planning.
- OPEN QUESTION: Which three games? (business decision; Main Street noted).
- OPEN QUESTION: Final definition of the second trigger achievement (suggestion above; confirm at planning).
data.title: Achievement give-aways: unlock three games when achievements are achieved (reuse follow-on-Steam mechanism)

# Task: Delete the retired `tableau-card-engine-core` repository

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer, once the merged-core epic (`CG-0MUJ0IAJM009X0Q2`) is complete
and released, the retired `tableau-card-engine-core` repository is deleted from
GitHub, so that exactly one core repository (`Tableau-Card-Engine`) exists and
no one can clone or mistake the old core for the current one.

## Discovery

Discovered during F6 (Retire tableau-card-engine-core, `CG-0MUJ1689Z007M58X`) of
the Option A merged-core epic. The operator chose to **archive now, delete
later**: the repository was archived on 2026-09-27 (verified
`gh api repos/TheWizardsCode/tableau-card-engine-core` → `archived: true`) but
not deleted, so that historical pins and forks keep resolving while the
merged-core refactoring is still in flight.

`discovered-from:CG-0MUJ0IAJM009X0Q2`

## Dependency

**Blocked by `CG-0MUJ0IAJM009X0Q2`** (the merged-core epic). Do not delete until
the epic — including F7 end-to-end verification and its release — is complete,
so the old repository remains available as a fallback during verification.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `Tableau-Card-Engine` HEAD has no remaining functional reference to
   `tableau-card-engine-core` (docs may keep annotated historical/provenance
   notes).
2. `gh api repos/TheWizardsCode/tableau-card-engine-core` returns HTTP 404
   (repository deleted).
3. The deletion is recorded in `docs/dev/merged-core-repoint.md` (and the F6 /
   parent work-item comments) with the date and the `gh` command used.
4. Archiving is confirmed done beforehand (it already is) so the delete is the
   only remaining external step.

## Minimal Implementation

```bash
# 1. Confirm still archived and the epic is released
gh api repos/TheWizardsCode/tableau-card-engine-core --jq '.archived'   # expect: true

# 2. Delete (requires the delete_repo scope: gh auth refresh -s delete_repo)
gh repo delete TheWizardsCode/tableau-card-engine-core --yes
gh api repos/TheWizardsCode/tableau-card-engine-core                     # expect: 404

# 3. Update docs/dev/merged-core-repoint.md: replace the "retained archived"
#    note with a completed-deletion record (date + command + 404 evidence).
```

**Key Files:** `docs/dev/merged-core-repoint.md`, `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`.

**Deliverables:** The deleted repository plus a reference-clean, documented tree.

## Constraints

- Requires a `gh` token with the `delete_repo` scope (`gh auth refresh -s delete_repo`).
- Irreversible: the old filtered-history pin `2e9fc0e5` and any pre-repoint game
  commits referencing the old `./core` URL will stop resolving.
- Push to `dev` only; `main` is promoted by the ship skill.
## Related work (automated report)

- **CG-0MMJ8S9850MV4L0A** – Engine Component Sketches: ChallengeSystem & DifficultyPresets (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MUA14D390010P9H** – Test review: strip source-grep 'module isolation' blocks from 3 core-engine tests (completed)

- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, already, api, architecture, auth (+84 more)

# Feature: Ship the ToneForge runtime synth module everywhere (commit it)

## Goal (user story)

As a player/tester running TCE in **any** environment — the launcher dev server,
a game-repo dev server, the built `dist/` (GitHub Pages), or the Electron
bundle — Main Street's ToneForge-backed synthesis audio works out of the box,
without anyone having to install the `tf` CLI or run `npm run tf:generate`
first.

## Context

Today the runtime synth module is generated on demand and never shipped:

- `scripts/tf-generate-synths.sh` writes `build/tf-synths/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs`
  (and a metadata module + WAVs + JSON) and **hard-fails** (`exit 1`) if the
  `tf` CLI is not on `PATH`.
- `build/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:15`) and Vite only copies `public/` into
  `dist/`, so the artefact is reachable on the dev server (which serves
  repo-root files) but **absent from `dist/` and the Electron bundle**.
- The runtime pre-checks `/build/tf-synths/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` and,
  when missing, logs `[MainStreet] ToneForge synth module not found …`
  (`src/tf/mainStreetTfModule.ts`).
- The decision recorded in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (§ToneForge Audio Generation) and
  `docs/the-build/audio.md` is explicitly **"we do not commit generated tf
  artifacts"** — this work item reverses that for the runtime module.
- CI never installs ToneForge, so generating at build time cannot work there.

The generated runtime module is **static JavaScript** (hard-coded Tone.js
factories) whose only runtime dependency is `tone`, which is already a shipped
dependency. It therefore does not need `tf`, WAVs, or network access at runtime.

## Proposed approach (confirm during planning)

1. Make the generated **runtime synth module** a source-controlled artefact so
   it is present in every checkout and copied into every build. Likely:
   generate/commit it at a path the runtime already serves
   (`public/build/tf-synths/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` in the launcher keeps
   the existing `/build/tf-synths/…` URL unchanged), or place it with the
   Main Street game assets and compose it via
   `repo-layout.json → gameAssets` (CG-0MUKYCG9L00587FA), updating the default
   URL.
2. Make `scripts/tf-generate-synths.sh` **fail-open**: a missing `tf` CLI is a
   warning/regeneration hint, never a build failure. `npm run build`/`dev` must
   not depend on `tf` and must not be changed to run generation.
3. Decide what is committed vs generated: commit the runtime module (and
   evaluate the metadata module); keep WAV/JSON generated output out of source
   control.
4. Update the docs to state which artefact is committed and how to regenerate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Clean checkout, no `tf`, no generation:** with the `tf` CLI absent and
   `npm run tf:generate` never run, `GAMES_CONFIG=full npm run dev` serves the
   runtime synth module at the exact URL `loadMainStreetTfModule()` requests,
   Main Street logs **no** `ToneForge synth module not found` warning, and
   synth-mapped SFX are active.
2. **Shipped build:** `GAMES_CONFIG=full npm run build` emits the module into
   `dist/` at the same URL path, and serving `dist/` (e.g. `npm run preview`)
   loads it with no warning. Same for `npm run build:electron`.
3. **Deterministic + single source of truth:** the committed module is the file
   the runtime loads; running `npm run tf:generate` (when `tf` is available)
   regenerates exactly that artefact with no drift, and the absence of `tf`
   never fails `npm run build` or `npm run dev`.
4. **Test coverage:** a unit test asserts the runtime default URL resolves to an
   on-disk artefact that is included in the public/build output, and that the
   module exports `TF_RUNTIME_MODULE`/`factories` including the expected keys
   (`card-draw`, `card-slide`, `card-place`, `card-discard`,
   `card-coin-collect`, `ui-notification-chime`, `card-table-ambience`,
   `construction-hammer`, `construction-saw`, `construction-lite-hammer`,
   `construction-lite-saw`, `crowd-cheer`).
5. **Docs:** `docs/DEVELOPER.md` §ToneForge Audio Generation and
   `docs/the-build/audio.md` no longer claim the runtime module is uncommitted;
   they state which artefact is source-controlled and how to regenerate it.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- Committing WAV or JSON generation output (binary/large) is out of scope.
- If the module must also be present in the **standalone `tce-main-street`
  repo**, that is a cross-repo follow-up; record it as a child/spin-off if the
  chosen placement does not cover it.

## Related

- Reverses the "do not commit generated tf artifacts" decision in
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md` / `docs/the-build/audio.md`.
- Prior work: CG-0MOIY2VV200658OX (TF output spike + spec, open questions #2/#4),
  CG-0MOIY3MSR008EH0I (npm script + docs), CG-0MOIXHOWP003Y6E0 (runtime
  synthesis).
- Sibling asset composition: CG-0MUKYCG9L00587FA.
- Discovered-from: CG-0MUKYCG9L00587FA.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MUG2ZK91003JCLC** – Dynamic ESM import & scene registration (open)
- **CG-0MSXL2MKO0005R6I** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManager.ts:1 — Expected a module name (invalid-syntax) (completed)
- **CG-0MSMDZEDN002MN8L** – GitHub Actions Windows binary job (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mukycg9l00587fa, absent, acceptance, access, active (+203 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, access, active, already (+159 more)
- `README.md` — matched: absent, access, active, also, approach (+128 more)
data.title: Ship the ToneForge runtime synth module everywhere (commit it)

## Goal

Freeze the interfaces and pure logic for achievement-triggered game give-aways so the rest of the feature can be built and tested with no Steam, Electron, or real launcher.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `GiveawayRule` (target game id + required achievement ids) and `GiveawayRuleSet` are typed and documented in `electron/achievement-giveaways.ts`; no game title is hard-coded in logic.
- Pure `evaluateGiveaways(unlockedAchievementIds, rules, alreadyUnlockedGameIds)` returns `{ gameId, unlocked, reason, missingAchievementIds }[]` with a discriminated `reason`.
- A unified multi-game `ContentUnlockStore` (memory + file implementation, corrupt-file-safe) generalises the existing single-game `UnlockStore`; the file store never throws.
- Unit tests cover: all required achievements met unlocks once; a subset blocks with `missingAchievementIds`; idempotent repeat; unknown/empty config is a no-op; a corrupt file degrades to empty state.
- Tests pass under `--project unit`.

## Key Files

- `electron/achievement-giveaways.ts` (new) — types + pure evaluation.
- `electron/steam-follow.ts` — share the persistence store as a multi-game store.
- `tests/steam-giveaways/giveaway-contract.test.ts` (new)

## Deliverables

Contract module, unified multi-game unlock store, unit tests.
data.title: Give-away unlock contract and deterministic fakes (test-first)

## Goal

Make "won a game" a first-class, engine-generic achievement event so the give-away triggers have a real, Steam-free source.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AchievementSystem` (or a documented thin extension) gains an idempotent game-outcome surface (e.g. `onGameOutcome({ gameId, outcome })`) that unlocks mapped achievements via the existing `AchievementSink`; zero Steam/Electron imports.
- The launcher manifest defines `first-win` and `second-distinct-game-win` meta-achievements (titles, descriptions, hidden flags) and the outcome-to-achievement mapping is engine-generic.
- "Second distinct game" logic only unlocks after wins in two different game ids; re-wins of the same game do not.
- `SteamAchievementService` idempotence and offline paths are reused unchanged for the meta-achievements.
- Unit tests cover outcome-to-unlock, distinct-game counting, idempotence, and no-op for unknown outcomes; pass under `--project unit`.

## Key Files

- `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts`
- `src/core-engine/index.ts`
- `electron/achievement-manifest.json`
- `tests/steam-achievements/achievement-outcome.test.ts` (new)

## Deliverables

Engine outcome surface, manifest meta-achievements, unit tests.
data.title: Engine game-outcome surface and cross-game meta-achievements

## Goal

Have Golf, Coloretto and Lost Cities report their terminal win outcome through the engine-generic contract, with no Steam SDK code in any game module.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of `../tce-golf`, `../tce-coloretto`, `../tce-lost-cities` calls the engine game-outcome surface on a completed win, using the same `gameId` as the launcher catalog/manifest.
- No Steamworks or Electron import appears in any game repo.
- In the browser/headless build the call is a no-op (no-op sink) and gameplay is unaffected.
- Each game repo's unit tests cover win-to-outcome reporting.
- The change is committed and pushed to each repo's `dev` branch (never `main`) and recorded on this item; tests pass under `--project unit` in each affected repo.

## Key Files

- `../tce-golf/src/scenes/GolfScene.ts`
- `../tce-coloretto/src/scenes/ColorettoScene.ts`
- `../tce-lost-cities/src/scenes/LostCitiesScene.ts`
- `../tce-golf/src/GolfAchievements.ts` (new per-repo reporting helper)

## Deliverables

Cross-repo outcome wiring + tests on `dev`, with results recorded here.

## Goal

A main-process service that evaluates the give-away config against locally-unlocked achievements and persists game unlocks through the shared store, reachable from the renderer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `GiveawayService` reads `SteamAchievementService.getUnlocked()`, evaluates the F1 contract against the give-away config, and persists unlocks to the unified `ContentUnlockStore`; it runs on launch and after each achievement unlock and never throws.
- `SteamFollowService` and `GiveawayService` share one unlock store so the Game Selector has a single source of truth; existing follow unlock behaviour is preserved and its existing tests still pass.
- IPC channels plus `electron/preload.cjs` expose give-away status/progress and a refresh call; channel names stay in sync and every handler is total.
- With Steam, the manifest, or the config absent the service degrades to a safe no-op (no fabricated unlock, no crash) and the web build is unaffected.
- Unit tests (mocked sources/stores) cover launch evaluation, post-unlock evaluation, idempotence, cross-launch persistence, and missing-dependency degradation; pass under `--project unit`.

## Key Files

- `electron/achievement-giveaways.ts`
- `electron/steam-achievements-ipc.ts`
- `electron/steam-follow-ipc.ts`
- `electron/preload.cjs`
- `electron/main.ts`
- `tests/steam-giveaways/giveaway-service.test.ts` (new)

## Deliverables

Give-away service, unified store wiring, IPC/preload surface, unit tests.
data.title: Give-away service with unified unlock persistence and IPC

## Goal

Show locked give-away games in the Game Selector with the milestones still required, and unlock them live when the triggers are met.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A unified lock computation consumes follow + give-away status and returns, per gated game, a lock reason and progress (remaining milestone titles/count); existing follow lock behaviour is preserved.
- `GameSelectorScene` renders SLL-compliant locked cards with progress (e.g. "1 of 2 milestones") and updates when a give-away unlocks; overlay/label objects follow the documented depth/parenting conventions.
- In a plain browser (no bridge) no game is locked and the app is fully playable.
- Unit tests cover mixed states (follow-unlocked, achievement-partial, achievement-complete, base content) and a browser test covers the rendered locked/progress state.
- Tests pass under `--project unit` and `--project browser`.

## Key Files

- `src/ui/steam-lock.ts`
- `src/ui/steam-giveaways-client.ts` (new)
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts`
- `tests/ui/steam-lock.test.ts`
- `tests/ui/GameSelectorGiveaways.browser.test.ts` (new)

## Deliverables

Unified lock model, renderer client, selector UI, unit + browser tests.

## Goal

Record the producer's decision — three give-aways (Golf, Coloretto, Lost Cities) triggered by "win your first game" plus "win in a second distinct game" — as versioned, game-agnostic config with drift detection.

- `electron/achievement-giveaways.json` lists exactly the three games (`golf`, `coloretto`, `lost-cities`) with their required achievement ids, plus a `_comment` recording the rationale and the no-overlap-with-the-follow-bonus (Feudalism) rule.

- A validator detects config drift — unknown game id, unknown achievement id, and overlap with the follow bonus — and an automated test fails on each case.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `README.md` document the config format, how to add/retarget a give-away, and the business-decision process.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (planning round, resolved)

- Q1: "Which three games are the give-aways?" — Answer (user): "Golf, Coloretto and Lost Cities". Source: interactive reply (2026-09-30). Final: {golf, coloretto, lost-cities}. Rationale: genre spread, excludes the follow-on-Steam bonus (Feudalism), each has a terminal win/lose outcome.
- Q2: "Final second trigger achievement?" — Answer (user): "recommended". Final: **"Win your first game in a second distinct game"** (paired with "win your first game"). Source: interactive reply (2026-09-30).

data.comment:
## Producer answers — blocking questions cleared (2026-09-30)

Interactive producer replies:

- **Q1 — Steam environment / logged-in assumption:** *"Do not assume client is logged in, rescope."* → P1's empirical ACs are **rescoped**: the probe/detection must be robust when Steam is running but **no user is logged in** (resolve `IsFollowing`, return `false` within a bounded timeout, never crash, never fabricate `true`). Real-session boolean verification is consolidated into **P6** (operator-run).
- **Q2 — chain continuation:** *"yes"* → P2–P4 may proceed against the frozen interface (**Option A**, interface `SteamFriends017`, async `FriendsIsFollowing_t` / callback 345) using fakes; real-session verification stays in P6.
- **Q3 — decision confirmation:** *"confirmed"* → **Option A** (custom N-API addon) confirmed, including the R1 mitigation plan (shared `CCallback` / `SteamAPI_ManualDispatch` rather than `GetAPICallResult` polling if the `steamworks.js` callback pump conflicts).

Consequences:
- P1 rescoped (see updated description/ACs) and unblocked.
- P2–P4 implementation authorised.
- A **no-logged-in** requirement is added to the detection contract: `isFollowing` must return `false` (not throw) when the Steam client is running without a logged-in user, and the capability flag must not claim automatic detection unless a real check is available.
- P6 remains the operator-run real-account end-to-end verification.
